notes: EXAM CODES VERIFIED AGAINST AWS ITSELF (2026-09-13). SAA-C03 is STILL the current Solutions Architect Associate exam - it has NOT been replaced. A search result claiming 'SAA-C04, released March 2024' came from an SEO content farm (citadelcloudmanagement.com) and is false: aws.amazon.com/certification/certified-solutions-architect-associate/ and the AWS docs exam guide both still resolve to solutions-architect-associate-03, and the AWS 'coming soon' page lists no SAA update. Do not let that claim reach the site.
SAP-C02 is still the current Solutions Architect Professional exam code; AWS lists no SAP-C03.

SCS-C03 IS NOW LIVE for AWS Certified Security - Specialty, replacing SCS-C02. Confirmed at docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-certification/latest/security-specialty-03/, which includes an explicit 'Comparison of SCS-C02 and SCS-C03' appendix. Every AWS security exam-prep book currently in print targets SCS-C02 and is therefore one version behind; no SCS-C03 book exists yet. If the site states SCS-C02 anywhere as current, that is now wrong. The exact SCS-C02 retirement date could not be confirmed on any AWS page - do not publish a date for it.

The only AWS 'coming soon' exam change AWS currently advertises is CloudOps Engineer Associate SOA-C03 replacing SOA-C02 (Sept 2025) - not relevant to these eight slots but worth knowing if a SysOps slot is ever added.

AMAZON STATUS IS WEAK EVIDENCE AND MUST NOT BE TREATED AS VERIFICATION. Amazon returns HTTP 200 for deliberately bogus ASINs (0000000000 and 9999999999 both returned 200 in testing), so a 200 does not prove a book exists. A 404 IS meaningful, and exactly one candidate hit it: the Orange AVA SAP-C02 guide (ISBN-10 9348107801) has no US Amazon detail page - do not publish that affiliate link. HEAD requests are rejected by Amazon with 405, so these are ranged GETs with a browser user-agent. Where the identity of a derived ISBN-10 mattered most, the Amazon page title was read back and matched: 1098119061 = DDIA, 1966280009 = Team Topologies 2nd Edition, 1950508943 = The Phoenix Project. Amazon began throttling after roughly fifteen requests, so the remaining titles were not title-checked this way.

REAL VERIFICATION came from three independent directions per book: the Open Library /api/books record (title, authors, publisher, date, ISBNs), a publisher or retailer page (IT Revolution, Manning, Pearson, Packt, O'Reilly, orangeava.com, AbeBooks), and deterministic ISBN-13 to ISBN-10 check-digit recomputation. Every ISBN-10 computed independently matched the ISBN-10 that had been read off a retailer page, and every ISBN-13 passes checksum validation. No ISBN in this file was invented or guessed.

OPEN LIBRARY COVERS ARE MISSING FOR 13 OF 24 CANDIDATES. Both the ISBN-13 and the ISBN-10 cover URLs were tested; where the ISBN-13 returned 404 (13 bytes), the ISBN-10 returned 404 as well, so there is no fallback within Open Library. The pattern is that recent Packt and O'Reilly titles have no cover art in Open Library. The site needs a placeholder or another cover source for: 9781837630004, 9781801813136, 9781835084236, 9789348107800, 9781098119065, 9781950508945, 9781966280002, 9781836641933, 9781098141936, 9781098146894, 9781098150358, 9781098116743, 9781805125440. A usable cover is >5 KB; the 11 that returned 200 ranged from 24,914 to 61,431 bytes.

BIGGEST CONTENT CHANGE: Designing Data-Intensive Applications 2nd edition is genuinely published (O'Reilly, March 2026, Kleppmann and Riccomini, 9781098119065). The author's own announcement page still reads as pre-release because it was written in March 2026, but the book is now listed and sold by O'Reilly, Blackwell's, Apple Books and Audible, and the Amazon dp page confirms the ISBN. Any existing link to the 2017 1st edition (9781449373320) should be replaced.

OTHER SUPERSEDED EDITIONS TO CHECK IF THE SITE ALREADY LINKS THEM: Fundamentals of Software Architecture 1st (9781492043454) is now 2nd (9781098175511, subtitle changed); Team Topologies 1st (9781942788812) is now 2nd (9781966280002, subtitle changed); The Phoenix Project '5th Anniversary Edition' (9781942788294) is superseded by the 2024 4th edition (9781950508945); AWS for Solutions Architects 2nd (9781803238951) is now 3rd (9781836641933) with a different author lineup; Designing Distributed Systems 1st is now 2nd (9781098156350); Infrastructure as Code 2nd is now 3rd (9781098150358).

EDITIONS EXPLICITLY CHECKED AND CONFIRMED AS STILL CURRENT (no newer edition exists): Terraform: Up & Running 3rd ed (the author's own site still presents it as current - there is no 4th edition), The DevOps Handbook 2nd ed, Accelerate (no 2nd ed), Software Architecture: The Hard Parts, Database Internals, Fundamentals of Data Engineering, Serverless Architectures on AWS 2nd ed, Site Reliability Engineering.

SLOT-2 IS GENUINELY THIN AND SHOULD BE PRESENTED AS SUCH. Only one current major-publisher SAP-C02 exam-prep book exists (the Packt Sard/Wadia guide). Sybex/Wiley publishes AWS Solutions Architect study guides at the Associate level only - the assumed 'Sybex SAP Professional Study Guide' does not exist. Pearson's AWS Solutions Architect author (Mark Wilkins) has written only at Associate level, and Marko Sluga's Pearson title is SysOps SOA-C02, a different certification. No Apress SAP-C02 title exists. Candidate 2 is supplementary reading rather than exam prep and candidate 3 is not Amazon-linkable, so treat slot-2 as one solid pick plus context.

TITLES DELIBERATELY REJECTED: the McGraw Hill AWS Certified Solutions Architect Associate All-in-One guide (latest edition targets SAA-C02, two codes behind, no SAA-C03 refresh exists); the McGraw Hill Security Specialty All-in-One guide (SCS-C01, two codes behind); the 2019 Pearson AWS SA Professional Cert Guide (SAP-C01 era, no named author); 'The CDK Book' (Gumroad ebook, no ISBN, cannot be catalogued or linked); Tutorials Dojo study guides (digital-only PDF licences with no ISBN of any kind, so they cannot use the /dp/<isbn10> link format); Neal Davis training-notes titles (979-prefix ISBNs, which have no ISBN-10 equivalent and therefore cannot form the required Amazon URL, plus an unconfirmed exam code); and several 2026-dated Amazon-only SAP-C02 and SAA-C03 titles by unknown authors with no publisher, which have the hallmarks of bulk or AI-generated certification books.

979-prefix ISBNs have no ISBN-10 equivalent by design. This is why some otherwise reasonable self-published titles cannot be used with the required amazonUrl format - it is a numbering-scheme fact, not a research gap.

FETCH BLOCKS ENCOUNTERED: wiley.com, packtpub.com, oreilly.com, blackwells.co.uk and mitpressbookstore all returned HTTP 403 to automated fetching, and the Google Books API returned 429 (quota exhausted). Open Library, Manning, Pearson IT Certification, orangeava.com, AbeBooks and the AWS documentation all fetched successfully and carried the load.

LOWEST-CONFIDENCE DATA POINTS, worth a re-check before publishing: the Sybex Security Study Guide 2nd edition year (Open Library says 2024, retailer metadata says July 2025) and its author lineup (two different lists circulate - Open Library's is used here); the Solutions Architect's Handbook 3rd edition author list (Open Library adds Kamal Arora, some retailers list only two authors); and System Design on AWS's year (AbeBooks 25 March 2025 vs Open Library 2024).
